speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin my assessment, have you experienced any trauma, recent surgeries, or ingestion of foreign objects? Additionally, when did these symptoms first start, and are they constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture)

The history of forceful retching following alcohol consumption, followed by sudden choking, coughing, and chest pain in a 51-year-old male is highly specific for esophageal rupture. I am requesting an immediate Chest_X-Ray and a contrast esophagram to confirm the diagnosis.
